insight.title: What holds the clouds in place
insight.subtitle: A quiet study of the invisible weight drifting above us.

sections.text: We look up and see white puffs drifting through the blue. They look like tufts of cotton or soft pillows of steam. You might think they weigh next to nothing. Yet, a single summer cloud can carry over a million pounds of water. It floats above your head, massive and silent, waiting for the wind.

How does something so heavy stay so high? The secret is in the heat. As the sun warms the earth, the air rises in gentle, invisible columns. These warm breaths act like giant hands. They cradle the tiny droplets, keeping them aloft. Gravity pulls, but the rising warmth provides a soft, constant lift.

This invisible balance happens every single day. It reminds us that there is a quiet strength in the air we breathe. Even when things feel light and effortless, there is often a great weight being held with grace. Life is full of these hidden miracles. We just have to remember to look up.

news.title: How Jagged Moon Dust Could Support Future Astronauts
news.description: Lunar dust can be a pain - but it’s also literally the ground we will have to traverse if we are ever to have a permanent human settlement on the Moon. In that specific use case, it’s clingy, jagged, staticky properties can actually be an advantage, according to a new paper, recently published in Research from researchers at Beihang University, who analyzed the mechanical properties of samples returned by Chang’e 6 mission to the far side of the Moon.
